subject: Renewal: term structure & phased capacity options
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Karen Lopez <karen.lopez@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: term structure & phased capacity options

Hi Karen —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Attached is an initial renewal draft (Atlas_2027_Renewal_Draft_v1.pdf) and the proposed phased capacity SOW (SOW_Phased_Capacity_Schedule.xlsx). High-level proposal for discussion:

- Term options: 24-month preferred with an optional 12-month alternate. We can do a multi-year price benefit if you commit 24+ months.
- Phased commits: Year 1 baseline commit (50% of peak forecast), Year 2 step-up to 75%, Year 3 full committed capacity. True-ups allowed at quarterly checkpoints.
- Auto-renew: default auto-renew at term end for an additional 12 months unless Atlas provides 60 days written notice. We can consider a 90-day opt-out window if that helps.
- Co-terming: we can align the commercial term to Atlas’ fiscal year (July 1) as requested; pricing will be pro-rated for the first partial term.

Questions for you: would Atlas be comfortable with a 24-month commit with a staggered ramp? Any regulatory approval timelines we should bake into the start dates?

Next steps: if the structure looks broadly acceptable, I’ll route to legal and finance for a redline and share a revised draft.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com
+1 (555) 321-7789

Attachments: Atlas_2027_Renewal_Draft_v1.pdf (PDF, 320KB); SOW_Phased_Capacity_Schedule.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)

From: Karen Lopez <karen.lopez@atlashealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:07:23 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: term structure & phased capacity options

Thanks, Ava. I reviewed the deck with our procurement and engineering leads — overall the phased approach makes sense, but two immediate concerns: 

1) Auto-renew: Procurement is wary of evergreen auto-renew clauses. We need an option that ensures Atlas has an explicit right to decline renewal for 90 days prior to renewal without penalty. 60 days feels tight for our RFP cycles.

2) Scale flexibility: our usage forecast could outpace the ramp in Year 2 if a feature rollout accelerates. Can we add a defined mechanism for mid-term scale-ups with pro-rated billing (and a cap on unit price for the first 12 months after scale)?

Also, legal asked for any security evidence we’ve shared previously (SOC 2 report) to attach to the new draft. Can you include that?

If you can update the draft with those two items, procurement can review the revised doc next week.

—Karen
Karen Lopez
Director, Cloud Architecture | Atlas Health
karen.lopez@atlashealth.com

Ben / Marissa —

Looping you in per Karen’s reply. Key asks from Atlas: 90-day opt-out window on auto-renew (procurement requirement) and a formal mid-term scale-up mechanism with pro-rated billing and a capped unit price for 12 months after any scale event. Also they requested SOC 2 evidence attached to the contract.

Can legal propose language to:
- Replace 60-day notice with 90-day written notice or a 90-day opt-out right with no penalty, and
- Add a short clause describing mid-term scale-up: customer may request immediate capacity increases; vendor will fulfill if capacity available; billing will be pro-rated for the remaining month and monthly unit price will be locked for 12 months from the scale event.

Finance: please confirm how you want to handle pro-rates and the mechanics for true-ups at quarter checkpoints.

Thanks,
Ava

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 08:22:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal: term structure & phased capacity options — proposed redlines

Ava —

Thanks for the ping. Legal reviewed and I suggest the following:

- Auto-renew: we can accept a 90-day opt-out. Proposed language: "This Agreement shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month terms unless either party delivers written notice of non-renewal at least ninety (90) days prior to the then-current term end. Customer may elect to decline renewal without penalty by providing written notice within that 90-day window."

- Mid-term scale-up: propose a short amendment to the SOW: "Customer may request increases to committed capacity at any time. Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to provision additional capacity within 30 days. Billing for added capacity will be pro-rated for the month of change and the per-unit price applicable to the scaled capacity will be fixed for twelve (12) months from the date of the scale event."

- Security evidence: attach SOC 2 Type II summary and a link to the security packet.

Finance: per Marissa (cc), we should also propose quarterly checkpoint true-ups with a mutual review scope. If the customer’s usage exceeds committed capacity at checkpoint, overage billing applies at the agreed overage rate and counts toward the next step-up.

I’ll generate a redline (Atlas_2027_Renewal_Draft_v2.pdf) with the above edits and send to Ava for customer review.

-Ben

Summary of changes:
- 24-month term (option to shorten to 12) with co-terming to Atlas fiscal year and pro-rated first partial term.
- 90-day written notice to decline auto-renewal (no penalty).
- Mid-term scale-ups allowed with 30-day provisioning target; billing pro-rated and unit price fixed for 12 months post-scale.
- Quarterly true-ups; overages bill at agreed overage rate and count toward phase step-ups.
- SOC 2 summary and security packet link included in the cover page.
